environment.description: Same Ktor microservice on ECS Fargate, but origin is isolated behind a CloudFront distribution with a custom origin access configuration. The ALB security group ingress is restricted to the AWS CloudFront managed prefix list (com.amazonaws.global.cloudfront.origin-facing) only. CloudFront is configured with a Trusted Key Group for signed URL validation — all requests to /api/v1/users/*/role require a valid CloudFront signed URL with a policy statement constraining the resource path and expiry to 30 seconds. The CloudFront distribution has a cache behavior for POST /api/v1/users/*/role with viewer protocol policy HTTPS-only and a Lambda@Edge origin-request function that validates the X-Service-Token against an IAM-authenticated Secrets Manager lookup (not the static check in the app code). The ADMIN_ENCRYPTION_KEY in this environment is a 256-bit key rotated every 24h via AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation Lambda, injected at container start via ECS secrets integration (arn:aws:secretsmanager:us-east-1:XXXX:secret:admin-key-RotatingXXX). Direct ALB access returns TCP RST for any source IP not in the CloudFront prefix list.

config.load_balancer: ALB with security group restricted to com.amazonaws.global.cloudfront.origin-facing prefix list

cloudfront.cache_behavior_post: Lambda@Edge origin-request validates X-Service-Token via Secrets Manager

config.encryption_key: 256-bit AES key, rotated every 24h via Secrets Manager automatic rotation
config.origin_access: CloudFront prefix list only, direct ALB access blocked at SG level
config.lambda_edge: origin-request function performs IAM-auth Secrets Manager GetSecretValue for token validation
